text:
Alex R: thinking out loud — can we split autoscale responsibilities into (1) an economic "soft reservation" layer and (2) a compact admission API for the runtime?
Maya S: interested. want to hear concrete boundaries.
Derek L: +1 on separation. soft reservations = bookkeeping for committed capacity, admission API = per-request decision.
Priya K: main worry is complexity: two systems -> more chances to drift on invariants. how do we prove safety?
Alex R: agree. invariant we need: admitted tokens <= committed capacity + burst credits. soft reserve must expose a simple predicate or numeric headroom value.
Maya S: example surface: runtime calls admit(tenant_id, token_cost) -> {allow: bool, reason: str, fallback_model: string?}. keep it tiny.
Derek L: and soft-reserve exposes get_headroom(tenant_id) -> int plus watch stream for changes. runtime uses the stream to preemptively route.
Priya K: what about warmup? starting a new GPU has a startup delta. admission should get a warmup_penalty param so callers can choose to queue vs fallback.
Alex R: nice. so API shape:
```
request = { tenant: "acme", tokens: 1024, warmup_tolerant: false }
response = { allow: true, fallback: "gpt-3-small", admission_trace_id: "abc123" }
```
Maya S: fallback_model hints are big win for graceful degradation. runtime can stream cheaper model while headroom increases.
Derek L: policy question: do we charge clients token credits as soon as admit() returns true, or only when request reaches GPU? double accounting race if admit succeeded but request dropped.
Priya K: we should reserve a short-lived provisional credit token. admit() returns a provisional_id that expires in ~30s unless committed by runtime. commit(token_id) finalizes. cancel(token_id) frees it.
Alex R: that solves races and lets operator reclaim leaks. infra-bot: created ticket #INF-827 for provisional-token TTL metrics. :white_check_mark:
Maya S: we discussed burst lanes before — should burst credits live entirely within soft-reserve, or split into a separate fast-path?
Derek L: keep burst accounting in soft-reserve but expose a fast admit_burst() that skips some checks for low-latency hot paths (still issues provisional_id).
Priya K: observability: every admit/commit/cancel must emit events with admission_trace_id + outcome. builds our SLO dashboards.
Alex R: fallback policy examples: 1) route to hosted cheaper model, 2) enqueue with estimated wait, 3) degrade quality via shorter max_tokens. runtime should implement these based on response.fallback.
Maya S: how do we handle cross-region capacity handoffs? if soft-reserve thinks headroom exists but provisioning time to other region is higher than SLO, runtime should prefer same-region fallback. we need region metadata in get_headroom.
Derek L: also preemption semantics — dedicated tenants might have preempt_shield flag. admission API must return preemptible: bool. runtime uses it to set QoS.
Priya K: operationally: operator needs tools to scan stale provisional tokens, reconcile leaked reservations to tenants, and simulate headroom forecasts. add admin endpoints.
Alex R: rollout plan: v1 small API (admit/commit/cancel/get_headroom + stream), instrument everything. run dedicated pool in canary with a few non-critical tenants.
Maya S: docs & SDK: keep client lib minimal. example Python: 
```python
with rdw.admit(tenant, tokens) as ticket:
    if ticket.allow:
        rdw.commit(ticket.id)
    else:
        fallback = ticket.fallback
```
Derek L: follow-ups: (a) finalize provisional TTL, (b) define admission error codes, (c) sampling for admission traces.
Priya K: + add regression test: simulate 1000 concurrent admits and verify provisional accounting never exceeds committed+burst.
Alex R: action items: Maya write API proto doc, Derek implement provisional token store sketch, Priya add test plan, I'll draft rollout playbook.
Maya S: will do. tagging infra-bot for ticket linking.
infra-bot: ticket INF-827 created (provisional-token-ttl-metrics).
Derek L: quick note — keep admission path idempotent for retries (client may re-call admit after transient error). provisional ids should be dedupable via client-provided request_id.
Priya K: thanks everyone. happy if we try this then reconvene after 2-week canary. :rocket:
Alex R: agreed — reconvene in 2 weeks. thanks!
